component: Earliest bounded passport admission and canonical envelope Base64
constraints: Immutable UTF-8 input bounded to 65536 bytes and depth eight; duplicate rejection, safe integer tokens, closed fields, canonical payload and standard padded Base64.
One 64-byte Ed25519 signature; caller-provisioned policy, trusted time/floors and artifact identity. No network, private-key processing or authority grant.
No identified target hardware, memory budget, throughput acceptance limit or hard deadline.
alternatives: Python lexical JSON hooks, native-backed Base64 decode/re-encode equality and native signature verification.
Erlang/Elixir OTP JSON callbacks and Base64 binary APIs with an explicit canonical adapter.
Rust base64 engine with explicit padding/trailing-bit configuration and a bounded lexical adapter.
C#/F# .NET Convert codecs and token-oriented JSON with explicit strict-wire checks.
rationale: KEEP the bounded runtime after fresh source review: immutable inputs, lexical hooks and a narrow decode/re-encode equality predicate express this profile without custom codec arithmetic. No candidate has demonstrated a material advantage under the identified constraints.

FIX assurance coverage: all 17 preexisting signature verification methods survived in-memory removal of canonical Base64 equality. Two new methods reject 33 aliases which decode to the original signed payload/signature bytes; removing the guard now causes 33 assertion failures.

OTP and .NET are credible alternatives outside the component language, but codec decoding alone is not this strict wire profile. Rust exposes relevant strictness controls; no claim is made that its complete adapter cannot improve measured native-target constraints.
Only the current runtime and controlled guard removal were executed. No speed ranking, installed-tool preference, familiarity or rewrite-cost argument is used.
limits: Production runtime and wire contract unchanged. This is a test-coverage repair, not a demonstrated deployed exploit or complete cryptographic validation.
An initial excess-padding experiment was unsuitable because the local decoder already rejects it. Failure evidence is retained; pad-bit variants supply the successful guard-sensitivity test.
No physical, real-time, MLS/CNSA, availability, installed-product or whole-lane completion claim.
